rac1/pal.title: Ratchet & Clank
rac1/pal.note: The boot executable and all 19 level programs. Handwritten assembly and linker remnants count as finished; staged near misses (nonmatching/) give the fuzzy figure.

rac1/ntsc.title: Ratchet & Clank
rac1/ntsc.note: Lombyte commits no report: its CI publishes one on the project's progress branch, which `openrac.py progress --fetch` copies to progress/sources/. Byte-weighted over the boot executable and the 19 level programs.

rac1/pal1.title: Ratchet & Clank
rac1/pal1.note: The boot executable and all 19 level programs, counted with the primary's rules (config/versions/pal_v1/functions.tsv): a function is finished when the shared C, or this release's own definition in src/versions/pal_v1/, builds its bytes (tools/version_check.py).

rac2/ntsc.title: Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando
rac2/ntsc.note: Every distinct function of the boot executable and the 27 level programs counted once (a function many levels share is one function); matched when its C links into a program that equals retail.

rac3/ntsc.title: Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal
rac3/ntsc.note: rac3-decomp's NTSC-U report (SCUS_973.53_report): a C function counts as final only when every NTSC-U program that has it builds it from C (docs/versions.md, The counts).

rac4/ntsc.title: Ratchet: Deadlocked
rac4/ntsc.note: Functions are compared one by one with most 16-bit immediates masked (symbols, struct offsets and small constants are not checked), and nothing is linked yet, so this is a looser proof than the other games'. Overlay code identical to resident code is counted once.
